_instructions: Potomac Electric Power Company (Pepco), MARYLAND service territory only. Wires-only distribution utility in a restructured state: generation (Standard Offer Service, SOS) and transmission are pass-through charges set through PJM/FERC processes, not by this rate case. Distribution parameters sourced from MD PSC Case No. 9820, Order No. 92607 (28 Aug 2026) and its Appendices A and B, plus the case record (OPC Exhibit DMM-1). Load and customers from the MD PSC Ten-Year Plan (2025-2034), Dec 2025. Fields marked _VERIFY are derived or estimated; the note explains the derivation. Dollar values are nominal $M unless stated. Calibration worksheet: utilities/calibration/Pepco_MD.csv.
name: Potomac Electric Power Company (Pepco) - Maryland
territory: Most of Montgomery and Prince George's counties, MD (suburban Washington DC)
filing_case: MD PSC Case No. 9820, Order No. 92607 (final order 28 Aug 2026; historic test year ending 30 Sep 2025; rates effective 10 Aug 2026)
_capacity_note: Capacity cost read from shared/capacity_markets/PJM.json zone PEPCO: $333.44/MW-day (2027/28 BRA, RTO-wide cap) x 365 / 1e6 = $0.1217M/MW-yr. 2028/29 BRA cleared at $325.00 (cap). PEPCO zone includes Pepco DC; no MD-only price exists. In Maryland the PJM capacity cost sits in the SOS supply price, so the capacity pass-through saving is modelled on the supply side of the bill.
_supply_transmission_note: WIRES-ONLY: Pepco MD earns a return only on distribution rate base. Transmission is FERC rate base (formula rate, PJM OATT) and is billed in the SUPPLY section of the Maryland bill ($0.02101/kWh). SOS generation is procured by auction under PSC rules and passed through at cost. This model therefore places transmission inside supply_rate_kwh and outside delivery_share_rr; neither is affected by the distribution rate base.
_residential_kwh_note: 900 kWh/month is the benchmark the Maryland Office of People's Counsel (OPC) uses for Pepco bill comparisons (opc.maryland.gov, Pepco rates page, Oct 2026). Actual Pepco MD residential average is ~825 kWh/month (5,478 GWh / 553,607 residential customers / 12; MD PSC Ten-Year Plan App. Tables 1(b)(i)-(ii), 2024). 900 chosen for comparability with Maryland public messaging.
_rate_base_note: Order No. 92607 Appendix A: adjusted rate base $2,994,612k (MD distribution only; transmission is FERC rate base and excluded). Per-book rate base $3,038,275k; contested adjustments include removal of White Flint substation (-$128,845k), smart fault sensors (-$843k) and 9655 reconciliation disallowances (-$12,041k).
_capex_VERIFY: Derived — no MD-only capital plan is published. Exelon Q4 2025 earnings 8-K (Ex. 99.2, 12 Feb 2026), Pepco slide: electric distribution capex $650M (2026E), $575M (2027E), $575M (2028E), $575M (2029E); transmission $325/400/400/400M; ~$3.9B total 2026-2029; 2025 rate base $8.4B, 77% distribution / 23% transmission. MD share = MD distribution rate base $2,994.6M / Pepco distribution rate base (0.77 x $8.4B = $6,468M) = 46.3%. MD distribution capex = 46.3% x average($650,575,575,575M) = $275M/yr (2026 alone: $301M). Below the $300-375M first estimate because Pepco's 2027-29 distribution plan steps down. Order 92607 describes the programme as mainly reliability, aging underground cable and substation work (RMAs 1-4 'reliability plant'), i.e. largely NOT load-growth driven.
_revenue_VERIFY: Derived. total_revenue_m = core MD distribution revenue requirement + SOS supply and transmission at June 2026 rates. (1) Distribution RR, all-in: 'Total Distribution Revenues, Adjusted' $835.6M (Pepco TTYCF, OPC Exhibit DMM-1 Sched. A line 38) + authorised increase $50.9M = $886.5M. (2) 'Other Taxes' in that cost of service are $227.5M: MD distribution property tax $55.2M plus $172.3M of other taxes. Pepco's 2024 FERC Form 1 (filed with the MD PSC, pp. 262-263) itemises MD non-property taxes of $168.4M: Montgomery County fuel-energy tax $126.6M, MD gross receipts/franchise tax $28.4M, Universal Service Program $7.5M, PSC assessment $3.9M, environmental surcharge $1.9M, other $0.1M. The Prince George's County energy tax ($49.4M paid in 2024) is collected on a net basis and is not in Other Taxes. All of these except the PSC assessment are separately itemised bill charges. Applying the 2024 proportions to the test year, $168.2M (97.6%) is excluded and the PSC assessment stays in. Core distribution RR = $886.5M - $168.2M = $718.3M. (3) Supply + transmission = 13,280 GWh (2026 net-of-DSM sales) x $0.13269/kWh = $1,762.1M. Total = $2,480M. Above the rough $2.1-2.2B first estimate because supply+transmission alone is ~13.3 c/kWh. Overstates Pepco's own revenue: retail-choice customers buy supply from third parties.
_roe_note: Order No. 92607: ROE 9.40% (Pepco requested 10.50%; prior authorised 9.50% in Case 9702). Capital structure 50.50% equity / 49.50% long-term debt at 5.00% cost of debt (Staff recommendation adopted). ROR 7.22% = 0.505 x 9.40% (4.747%) + 0.495 x 5.00% (2.475%). The model's COST_OF_DEBT default (5.0%) reproduces this exactly: WACC 7.222%.
_customers_note: MD PSC Ten-Year Plan (2025-2034), Dec 2025, read directly: 604,408 MD customers at 31 Dec 2024 (553,607 residential, 50,624 commercial, 177 other; App. Table 1(b)(i)); 2026 forecast 619,357 (Table 2), used as the start-year value.
_peak_note: MD PSC Ten-Year Plan, read directly: Pepco MD summer peak 3,630 MW gross / 3,209 MW net of DSM (2025); 3,644 MW gross / 3,222 MW net (2026) (App. Tables 3(a)(i)-(ii)); 2034 3,738 MW gross (CAGR 2025-2034 0.33%/yr). Summer-peaking (winter 2026: 2,642 MW). Gross used to match the convention for Con Edison and Dominion (system peak before programme impacts); the 422 MW gross-net gap in 2026 is existing EmPOWER/DSM peak savings.
_energy_note: MD PSC Ten-Year Plan (2025-2034), read directly from the tables: 13,106 GWh MD sales in 2024 (5,478 residential, 7,571 commercial, 57 other; App. Table 1(b)(ii)). Forecast gross of DSM: 13,674 GWh (2025), 13,618 GWh (2026) (App. Table 2(a)(i)); net of DSM: 13,337 GWh (2025), 13,280 GWh (2026) (App. Table 2(a)(ii)). Net-of-DSM forecast CAGR 2025-2034 is 0.04%/yr — PEPCO MD IS ESSENTIALLY FLAT, unlike Dominion VA. Net (billed) sales used here.
_tariff_VERIFY: INCLUSION RULE (same for delivery_rate_kwh and the distribution revenue requirement): costs recovered through Pepco's base distribution charges are IN; taxes and surcharges itemised separately on the bill are OUT. IN: Schedule R customer charge and volumetric distribution charge (which recover O&M, depreciation, return, property tax, income tax and the PSC assessment). OUT of both: Montgomery and Prince George's county energy taxes (Montgomery $0.0113227/kWh, Prince George's $0.013663/kWh), MD gross receipts/franchise tax, Universal Service Program charge, environmental surcharge, and the EmPOWER Maryland surcharge ($0.020618/kWh, Jan 2026; cut under the Utility RELIEF Act 2026, OPC cites >= $150/yr per household). The modelled bill therefore understates the actual bill by roughly 3.4-4.0 c/kWh. Rates, per Maryland OPC Pepco rate pages: customer charge $8.44/month; distribution $0.04328/kWh (winter / Oct 2026 listing). Summer (Jun-Oct) distribution $0.08760/kWh is from the pre-order Schedule R and was not confirmed on OPC's current page. Season-weighted (5 summer / 7 winter months) = $0.06175/kWh; plus the Order 92607 residential impact of +$3.94/month at 900 kWh (+$0.00438/kWh) = $0.0661/kWh. _VERIFY: post-order compliance tariff (rates effective 10 Aug 2026) not located; confirm the volumetric rates and whether the $8.44 customer charge changed.
_supply_rate_note: SOS residential generation $0.11168/kWh (Jun-Sep 2026) + transmission $0.02101/kWh = $0.13269/kWh. For reference: Oct 2026-May 2027 SOS $0.12670 (+13%), giving $0.14771 with transmission; 12-month Jun 2026-May 2027 weighted average $0.14270. Sources: OPC Pepco rate page (Oct 2026); Pepco SOS filings as reported by EnergyChoiceMatters (22 Apr 2026). The June value is kept as the 2026 anchor.
_delivery_share_note: Derived: core distribution RR $718.3M / total_revenue_m $2,480M = 0.2896; reproduces $718.2M in 2026. Same inclusion rule as delivery_rate_kwh (see _tariff_VERIFY). Tax classification from Pepco's 2024 FERC Form 1; the test-year split applies 2024 proportions.
_property_tax_note: Case record (OPC Exhibit DMM-1, RMA 26 workpaper): MD distribution property tax $55.186M in the test period; $59.091M on the FY2026 assessment (Pepco: +10.6% over FY2025; RMA 26 accepted by the Commission subject to removing disallowed plant). Rate = $59.091M / $2,994.6M adjusted rate base = 1.97%.
_income_tax_note: Derived: federal 21% + Maryland corporate 8.25% x (1 - 0.21) = 27.52% combined. Gross-up 1/(1-0.2752) = 1.3796; the order's conversion factor 1.3972 is 1.0127x that, consistent with revenue-related deductions (uncollectibles, PSC assessment) of ~1.3%. Not used by the engine (the model's return is after-tax WACC); recorded for calibration.
_dc_VERIFY: LOW confidence. Pepco MD's own forecast shows flat sales, so data-centre load in the MD territory is small today. PJM's 2026 load forecast includes a PEPCO-zone data-centre adjustment, but that zone also covers Pepco DC and SMECO. The proposed Brightseat Tech Park (Landover, Prince George's, up to ~820 MW) was paused in Sept 2025 pending the county task force. Base case 25 MW growing 5%/yr; notebook Section 12f runs 0 MW and an 800 MW step in 2032. In the engine a step raises peak in full but distribution capex (and NWS eligibility) only through dc_distribution_share (25%): large-load connections are largely transmission-connected or CIAC/customer-funded, and the Utility RELIEF Act 2026 lowered the large-load tariff threshold to 25 MW, requires large loads to pay a dedicated infrastructure tariff and assigns PJM data-centre capacity costs to data centres. _VERIFY the 25% distribution share against Pepco's large-load tariff filings.
_storage_VERIFY: Placeholder 15 MW. Next Generation Energy Act 2025 sets a 150 MW goal for distribution-connected storage; PSC Order No. 92281 (Apr 2026) approved BGE, Pepco, Delmarva and Potomac Edison RFPs for a first tranche of ~50 MW. Pepco's share of that tranche (~10.5 MW proposed) was not confirmed from a primary source. Behind-the-meter storage in the territory unknown.
_ev_VERIFY: MDOT MVA open data (opendata.maryland.gov, dataset qtcv-n3tc), Aug 2026: 160,773 BEV+PHEV registered in Maryland; Montgomery 49,599 + Prince George's 18,718 = 68,317 (42.5%). Pepco serves most but not all of both counties (Potomac Edison serves part of Montgomery; BGE and SMECO parts of Prince George's): territory share assumed 85% of the two-county total = 0.361 of statewide EVs. Used by the engine as ev_territory_share against the Maryland EV_ADOPTION_CURVE in the notebook.
_ev_managed_note: PLACEHOLDER 5%. No published Pepco MD figure for the share of EVs on managed charging was found. Pepco's managed charging is pilot-stage: the Case 9820 record includes EV Phase I and Phase II pilot cost recovery (OPC Exhibit DMM-1, RMA 12 and FFTY RMAs 7-8), and the DRIVE Act flexible-load proposal (Case 9761) is not approved. Set below the other modelled utilities (Con Edison 10%, RG&E 8%, Dominion 6%) to reflect that. Replace with Pepco EV programme enrolment / registered EVs when available.
_nws_VERIFY: MOST UNCERTAIN. Start 18%, ceiling 30% of distribution capex NWS-eligible. Flat load means little growth-driven capex; most spending is reliability and asset condition (Order 92607, RMAs 1-4). Capacity-driven projects do exist: White Flint ($164.9M per Pepco) was built for a forecast Parklawn overload, and MEA testified an NWA portfolio at 13-25% of installed cost was feasible. Read by the Maryland notebook into NWS_ELIGIBLE_CAPEX_SHARE_START / _MAX.
_grid_utilization_VERIFY: No real Pepco grid-utilization data used. COMAR 20.50.15 (Electric System Planning, effective 24 Nov 2025) requires feeder-level information where constraints exist; Pepco's first Annual Plan Update / Electric System Plan should replace this assumption with real constraint data once filed. NEEDS REAL GRID UTILIZATION DATA.
_dist_upgrade_VERIFY: Placeholder $2.2M/MW: dense suburban, significant underground; between RG&E (1.5) and Con Edison (4.0). White Flint cross-check (Order 92607): Pepco cost $164.9M, MEA figure $254.2M. Per MW of Parklawn firm capacity (82.5 MW): $2.00M / $3.08M. Per MW of capacity added (combined 177.5 MW - 82.5 MW = 95 MW): $1.74M / $2.68M. Per MW of the forecast overload actually addressed (11.9 MVA, treated as ~MW): $13.9M / $21.4M — the gap is the oversizing the Commission found imprudent.
_flexible_load_note: Reference ceiling for the flexible fleet: Pepco's DRIVE Act proposal (PSC Case 9761) would aggregate up to 185 MW of flexible load (customer batteries, EVs, thermostats; existing EmPOWER load-management moved in). Not approved; the PSC asked utilities to scale up proposals (Oct 2025) and postponed the March 2026 hearing. A revised 2026 figure was not found.
_notes: Disallowances recorded in Order No. 92607: (1) White Flint substation capital, $164.9M project family, removed from plant in service (rate base -$128.8M) as imprudent — Pepco did no formal NWA analysis; Parklawn's 82.5 MW is not forecast to be exceeded through 2034. (2) RMAs 3 and 4 post-test-year plant (Apr 2026-Jul 2027) excluded. (3) RMA 25 inflation adjustment to non-labor O&M rejected. (4) RMA 27 forecast property tax rejected. (5) $1.1M smart fault sensors moved from rate base to a regulatory asset. Revenue increase $50.946M of $119.876M requested (originally $133M forecast-test-year filing, withdrawn after the Utility RELIEF Act). Operating income at approved rates ~$179.7M adjusted (required $216.2M); conversion factor 1.3972; residential bill impact +$3.94/month. Phase II opened for Utility RELIEF Act compensation compliance. Prior case: Case 9702, Order No. 91181 (10 Jun 2024), $44.6M, ROE 9.50%, multi-year plan reduced to one year.

forward_assumptions._note: Forward assumptions for the layer engine (engine/layers.py). v1.0 / CORRECTED do not read this section. Levels: for layer assumptions 'low' gives customers a SMALLER shared-savings effect and 'high' a LARGER one. For growth assumptions (projection, system_needs, capacity price growth) low/high = lower/higher growth. Scenarios (Cautious / Central / Ambitious) set the programs, deferral and load_enabled layers together and hold growth assumptions and the utility share at central.

Cautious.description: Today's programs grown modestly, no flexible connections, high cost per kW-year, low locational match; growth and utility share central.

Central.description: Every assumption at central; flexible MW anchored to Maryland DRIVE Act and NGEA storage.

Ambitious.description: DOE national range (20% of peak) or the state anchor if higher, low cost per kW-year, high locational match, more flexible connections; growth and utility share central.

ev_hub_share.unit: share of EV peak growth at large charging hubs

flex_conn_share.unit: share of new distribution-connected DC and EV-hub MW on flexible connections
flex_conn_share.source: Duke University Nicholas Institute, "Rethinking Load Growth" (Feb 2025): 76 / 98 / 126 GW of new large load could connect to the US bulk system with 0.25% / 0.5% / 1% of annual energy curtailed. Bulk-system study; evidence for distribution-level flexible connections is thinner. Central modest; Cautious zero.

flex_conn_peak_depth.unit: share of a flexible connection curtailable at network peak
flex_conn_peak_depth.source: Assumption: flexible connections accept full curtailment in constrained hours

flex_conn_energy_curtailed.unit: share of the flexible load's annual energy curtailed
flex_conn_energy_curtailed.source: Duke University Nicholas Institute, "Rethinking Load Growth" (Feb 2025): 76 / 98 / 126 GW of new large load could connect to the US bulk system with 0.25% / 0.5% / 1% of annual energy curtailed. ramp_pct_peak_dr.unit: maximum MW added per year, share of the utility's 2026 peak (null = no cap)
ramp_pct_peak_dr.source: Observed ramp: Pepco Energy Wise Rewards direct load control added 50 MW in 2010 (EmPOWER Maryland 2011 report, Table 16) and 44 MW in 2011 (2012 report, Table 16), its fastest build-out = 50 / 3,644 MW Pepco MD peak = 1.37% of peak per year (central). Long-run 2009-2025: 0 to 247 MW (2026 EmPOWER report, Table 13) = 14.5 MW/yr = 0.40% of peak per year (low, Cautious). High (Ambitious): no cap, the target path applies. Expressed as a share of each utility's 2026 peak

ramp_pct_peak_ev.unit: maximum MW added per year, share of the utility's 2026 peak (null = no cap)
ramp_pct_peak_ev.source: Observed ramp: Pepco Energy Wise Rewards direct load control added 50 MW in 2010 (EmPOWER Maryland 2011 report, Table 16) and 44 MW in 2011 (2012 report, Table 16), its fastest build-out = 50 / 3,644 MW Pepco MD peak = 1.37% of peak per year (central). Long-run 2009-2025: 0 to 247 MW (2026 EmPOWER report, Table 13) = 14.5 MW/yr = 0.40% of peak per year (low, Cautious). High (Ambitious): no cap, the target path applies. Expressed as a share of each utility's 2026 peak. No observed utility program ramp for this resource type in these territories; the Maryland DLC ramp is used as the closest analogue

ee_kw_per_mwh.unit: kW summer peak saved per MWh/yr of first-year savings
ee_kw_per_mwh.source: EmPOWER Maryland 2024 program year, independent evaluation (Guidehouse; 2026 EmPOWER Standard Report, p.21): verified gross first-year savings 861,804 MWh and 94.183 MW summer = 0.1093 kW per MWh (central); net 706,841 MWh and 68.514 MW = 0.0969 (low); reported (verified / realisation rates 0.89 energy, 0.83 demand) = 0.1172 (high). Replaces ee_peak_coincidence (central 1.0 = savings shaped like system load, ~2x higher)

deferral.label: Deferral: flexible headroom counted by the network planner

locational_match.unit: share of new firm MW located where growth capex is needed
locational_match.source: Assumption; feeder-level constraint data (e.g. COMAR 20.50.15 plans, DSIPs) should replace it

load_enabled.label: Load enabled: waiting load connects sooner without reinforcement

enable_share.unit: share of flexible headroom offered to waiting load first (rest to deferral)
enable_share.source: Setting: priority to connecting waiting load where the network is constrained

connection_cost_kw.unit: $ per kW connected, not covered by CIAC (2026 $)
connection_cost_kw.source: Assumption: connection works not paid by the customer

incremental_om_mwh.unit: $ per MWh served to enabled load (2026 $)

uplift_mode.source: Setting. 'derived': headroom = firm flexible MW x locational match + flexible connections; 'direct': assumed % uplift in existing network capacity (what-if)

direct_uplift_pct.unit: uplift in existing network capacity (direct mode)

customer_funded_share.unit: share of network upgrade cost per MW counted as connection cost avoided by new customers
customer_funded_share.source: Setting: upper bound (all upgrade cost for MW connected sooner or on flexible connections, at dist_upgrade_cost_per_mw). The share new customers pay through CIAC is tariff-specific; access metric only, not on the bill

capacity.label: Capacity: firm MW at the zonal price

price_growth.source: central = INFLATION_RATE (flat real); high = market file growth (5%); low = flat nominal

mechanism.label: Shared savings mechanism and earnings opportunity

utility_share.unit: share of savings pool (shared savings earnings)
utility_share.source: notebooks/GridDividend_Maryland.ipynb Section 1 UTILITY_SAVINGS_SHARE 0.30; guidance range 0.10-0.40 (low = larger utility share)

pool_basis.source: Setting. 'revenue_requirement' = reduction in distribution RR + program surcharges + capacity cost vs BAU (EE energy-purchase savings go wholly to customers); 'capex' = v1.0-style avoided-capex pool (upper bound)

wholesale_energy.label: Hook for a later step: wholesale energy price effects

roe.label: Hook for a later step: allowed ROE

network.label: Network: existing headroom, planning limit, constrained sub-band, reinforcement, flexibility targeting
network._note: Every headroom input. Set at three levels, highest wins: notebook NETWORK_OVERRIDES (Section 13) > scenarios[name]['network'] (value or low/central/high level) > these values. Dominion PUR-2026-00164 proxy throughout (_VERIFY) until this utility's feeder-loading data is found. Constrained sub-band on for Central (network block); Cautious and Ambitious keep it off through their scenario network values, so they are unchanged.

band_mode.unit: 'explicit' = the bands list; 'generated' = n_bands equal-capacity bands from mean_utilisation and utilisation_spread

bands.unit: bands of substation loading, most to least loaded: share of firm capacity, starting loading (network peak / firm capacity); growth_share and flex_share optional (default pro rata to load)
bands.source: Dominion Energy Virginia, Grid Utilization Metrics Proposal, SCC Case No. PUR-2026-00164 (filed 15 Oct 2026), Section 4.3: substation-transformer zones at their own local peak average 79.8% planning utilisation (78.3% general; capacity net of a 0.70 x largest-transformer N-1 reserve); 82 of ~1,900 feeders (4.3%) exceed 100% planning utilisation (load / (0.80 x rating - contract reserves)), the filing's definition of a constrained feeder. No published utility-wide loading distribution found: Pepco publishes hosting-capacity maps; no aggregate loading distribution found in Maryland PSC filings (COMAR 20.50.15 text not located); Dominion's measured distribution (the only US utility-wide figure found) is used as a proxy. Replace with utility data.

n_bands.source: Same count as the explicit bands (quintiles of firm capacity)

mean_utilisation.unit: capacity-weighted mean starting planning utilisation (network peak / planning capacity); null = bands as given (79.8%). Set a number to shift every band by one amount to that mean, each capped at 1.0 (load above the planning limit goes in the sub-band); generated mode uses it as the centre (null = the explicit bands' mean)
mean_utilisation.source: Dominion Energy Virginia, Grid Utilization Metrics Proposal, SCC Case No. PUR-2026-00164 (filed 15 Oct 2026), Section 4.3, Metric (i): substation-transformer zones at their own local peak average 79.8% planning utilisation (78.3% general utilisation) Dominion value used as a proxy until this utility's own feeder data is found.

utilisation_spread.unit: most minus least loaded band (generated mode; linear spread)
utilisation_spread.source: Derived from the explicit bands (1.00 - 0.63); the filing reports only the mean and the count of feeders above 100%, so the shape is assumed Dominion value used as a proxy until this utility's own feeder data is found.

planning_limit_factor.unit: planning capacity / feeder rating (planning utilisation = load / (factor x rating - contract reserves))
planning_limit_factor.source: Dominion Energy Virginia, Grid Utilization Metrics Proposal, SCC Case No. PUR-2026-00164 (filed 15 Oct 2026), Metric (iv): planning utilisation = (SCADA net load + DER generation + flexibility) / (0.80 x applicable feeder rating - contract reserves); the 0.80 factor reserves 20% of the rating for contingencies and distribution-automation transfers (not applied to data-centre, industrial or grouped single-customer feeders) Dominion value used as a proxy until this utility's own feeder data is found.

operating_limit.unit: operating limit as a multiple of planning capacity; null = 1 / planning_limit_factor (1.25 at 0.80). Existing load is served up to it
operating_limit.source: Derived: the full feeder rating relative to 0.80 x rating (contract reserves ignored) Dominion value used as a proxy until this utility's own feeder data is found.

subband_enabled.unit: per-utility switch: carve a constrained sub-band (load above the planning limit) out of the most loaded bands. On for Central (scenario None = Central); Cautious and Ambitious switch it off in their scenario network values

subband_load_share.unit: share of network load in the constrained sub-band
subband_load_share.source: Dominion Energy Virginia, Grid Utilization Metrics Proposal, SCC Case No. PUR-2026-00164 (filed 15 Oct 2026), Metric (iv): 82 of ~1,900 feeders (4.3%) exceed 100% planning utilisation at their local peak. Feeder share used as a proxy for load share Dominion value used as a proxy until this utility's own feeder data is found.

subband_utilisation.unit: starting planning utilisation of the constrained sub-band
subband_utilisation.source: Midpoint of the planning limit (1.00) and the operating limit (1.25); the filing gives only the count of feeders above 100%, not their loading Dominion value used as a proxy until this utility's own feeder data is found.

upgrade_delay_ordinary_years.unit: Upgrade Delay for Interconnection, ordinary new load (EVs, heat pumps, small business) in constrained areas: years from request to connection (fractional years split between the two whole years)
upgrade_delay_ordinary_years.source: No Pepco Maryland timeline found: Maryland PSC, Electric System Planning report under PUA s. 7-802 (Dec 2025) describes PHI's 10-year feeder/substation forecasts and new-business short-term forecasts but no connection times. Con Edison guide used as proxy. Con Edison, E-Mobility Interconnection Guide: New & Upgraded Electric Service Overview (coned.com, rev. 30 Apr 2026): project timeline from service determination to energization, including any upstream utility modifications and transformer or feeder reinforcement: <300 kW overhead / <500 kW underground 4-6 months; 300-2,000 kW 12-18 months; 500-5,000 kW network and 2,000-10,000 kW 24-36 months; >8,000 kW high-tension 36+ months. Low 0.5 / central 1.5 / high 3.0 yr

upgrade_delay_large_years.unit: Upgrade Delay for Interconnection, large loads (data centres on the distribution system, fleet hubs) in constrained areas: years from request to connection
upgrade_delay_large_years.source: No Pepco Maryland timeline found: Maryland PSC, Electric System Planning report under PUA s. 7-802 (Dec 2025) describes PHI's 10-year feeder/substation forecasts and new-business short-term forecasts but no connection times. Con Edison guide used as proxy. Large loads: Con Edison guide low 2.0 yr (24 months), central 3.0 yr (36+ months, >8 MW); high 6.0 yr from Dominion Energy Virginia, Application for approval of large-load connection queue process standards, SCC Case No. PUR-2026-00011 (filed 2 Feb 2026), para. 5-6: ~25,000 MW of large-load delivery-point requests (>= ~100 MW, data centres) assigned projected connection dates through 31 Dec 2031; a further ~45,000 MW batched and still being studied; ~10 new requests (2,000-3,000 MW) a month

backlog_clearance_pct.unit: share of the outstanding constrained backlog (existing load above the planning limit) the utility clears per year, in service the following year; replaces clearing as soon as lead time and build rate allow
backlog_clearance_pct.source: No utility publishes a clearance rate for constrained feeders. Low 6%/yr: Dominion Energy Virginia, Application for approval of large-load connection queue process standards, SCC Case No. PUR-2026-00011 (filed 2 Feb 2026), para. 5-6: ~25,000 MW of large-load delivery-point requests (>= ~100 MW, data centres) assigned projected connection dates through 31 Dec 2031; a further ~45,000 MW batched and still being studied; ~10 new requests (2,000-3,000 MW) a month - about 25 of 70 GW given dates over the ~6 years to 2031, ~6% of the backlog a year (large loads, transmission). Central 20%/yr (backlog cleared in about 5 years) is an assumption between that and high 33%/yr (cleared within the 3-year central reinforcement lead time, close to the earlier model assumption)

constrained_build_priority.unit: constrained areas get build-rate priority: their upgrades are not capped by max_build_pct (false = backlog clearance and new-load upgrades together capped at max_build_pct of the band capacity per year)
constrained_build_priority.source: Model setting (overloaded feeders are relieved first for reliability)

planning_headroom.unit: firm network capacity above network peak, share
planning_headroom.source: No published system-wide figure. Con Edison publishes feeder hosting/load-capacity maps (coned.com/en/business-partners/hosting-capacity); Pepco must file feeder-level constraint data under COMAR 20.50.15. Neither is aggregated to a system headroom %.

reinforcement_lead_years.unit: years from order to in service
reinforcement_lead_years.source: Assumption: distribution feeder and substation reinforcement typically takes 2-5 years

max_build_pct.unit: maximum reinforcement ordered per year, share of capacity

seed_pipeline.unit: projects under way at 2026: 'derived' = the next lead-time years of network growth with planning headroom, allocated to bands by growth share (keeps the 2026 growth / asset-condition capex split independent of the bands); 'none'; or [{year, mw}]
seed_pipeline.source: Model calibration; no utility publishes its in-flight distribution capacity pipeline in MW

constrained_loading.unit: loading above which a band counts as constrained
constrained_loading.source: Dominion Energy Virginia, Grid Utilization Metrics Proposal, SCC Case No. PUR-2026-00164 (filed 15 Oct 2026), Section 4.3: substation-transformer zones at their own local peak average 79.8% planning utilisation (78.3% general; capacity net of a 0.70 x largest-transformer N-1 reserve); 82 of ~1,900 feeders (4.3%) exceed 100% planning utilisation (load / (0.80 x rating - contract reserves)), the filing's definition of a constrained feeder (constrained = above 100% planning utilisation)

flex_targeting_enabled.unit: site flexible headroom first in bands above their planning limit; false = pro rata (flex_share)
flex_targeting_enabled.source: Model setting (policy lever: locational targeting of flexibility)

flex_targeting_share.unit: maximum share of flexible headroom sited in bands above their planning limit when targeting is on (never more than the load above the limit); 1.0 = those bands first

capacity_carve_out.source: Price: PEPCO zone 2026/27 BRA $329.17/MW-day (MD PSC Ten-Year Plan Table 14). Peak: Pepco_MD.json peak_demand_mw. Residential share and customers: EIA-861 2024. Scaling: PJM forecast pool requirement 0.9401 (2028/29 BRA report). SOS prices include PJM capacity for the delivery year.
capacity_carve_out.method: Residential capacity obligation per customer = peak_mw x residential_share x obligation_scaling / residential_customers; $/month = obligation (kW) x price ($/kW-day) x 365/12. Assumes the residential share of the obligation equals its share of sales (residential load is peakier, so this likely understates it). The amount is moved out of the parent line(s); the total bill is unchanged.

starting_adjustments.name: Order No. 92607 residential increase (not yet billed)
starting_adjustments.source: MD PSC Order No. 92607 (Case 9820), Table 1: Commission-authorised residential bill impact +$3.94/month
starting_adjustments.note: Schedule R rates in effect 28 Aug-31 Oct 2026 are pre-case; the authorised increase is added here as an adjustment. The gross receipts surcharge applies to it.
